summary: download/offload/test surface for the model layer: list|status|stop|pull|test per stage (stt, ocr, vlm, enrich, triage, embed, rerank)
usage: plainkeep models list | status | stop [--all] [<model>] | pull [--stage <s>|--all] --approved | test <stage> [--model <m>] [--input <file>] --approved
reads: PLAINKEEP_OCR / PLAINKEEP_VLM / PLAINKEEP_ENRICH_MODEL / PLAINKEEP_EMBED_MODEL / PLAINKEEP_RERANK_MODEL env
writes: ollama's local model store (pull only; outside ~/plainkeep)
hints: Per-stage model management, env-config-driven (proposal docs/design/proposals/2026-07-07-search-enrichment-pipeline.md §2.1). `list` shows each stage's configured model, runtime, and whether it's pulled/available — pure probes, never loads a model. `status` is `ollama ps` (resident models). `stop [--all]` unloads a resident model (`ollama stop`) — free of --approved, it just reloads on next use. `pull [--stage <s>|--all]` and `test <stage> [--model <m>] [--input <file>]` both self-gate: without --approved they refuse with EXIT_CONFIRM(3) and print the exact re-run, because both can pull gigabytes; test then runs the stage's configured (or --model override) model on a sample/--input and prints output + timing, so you can A/B a candidate before adopting it by setting its env var. stt/rerank are pip-managed runtimes, not ollama models — pull skips them with a note. Common mistake: expecting `pull`/`test` to run without --approved — they never do, by design.

actions.name: list
actions.summary: each stage's configured model, runtime, and availability (pure probes)

actions.name: stop
actions.summary: unload a resident model (reloads on next use; no --approved)

actions.name: pull
actions.summary: download a stage's model (can be gigabytes); needs --approved

args.name: --stage
args.help: which stage's model to pull (omit with --all)

actions.name: test
actions.summary: run a stage's model on a sample/--input and print output + timing; needs --approved

args.name: --model
args.help: override the stage's configured model (A/B a candidate)
